snippets.output: The duration of seasonal influenza symptoms can vary depending on several factors, including an individual's overall health, age, and whether the individual has received the flu vaccine.
The acute symptoms of seasonal influenza typically last about 3 to 7 days in most healthy individuals.
Acute symptoms of seasonal influenza include fever, chills, muscle aches, and fatigue.
Some symptoms of seasonal influenza, such as cough and fatigue, can persist for up to two weeks or longer.

Young children, the elderly, and individuals with weakened immune systems may experience a longer duration of seasonal influenza symptoms and are at higher risk for complications from seasonal influenza.
Antiviral medications can reduce the duration of seasonal influenza symptoms by about one day if started within the first 48 hours of symptom onset.
